Novohrad Volynskyy New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Novohrad-Volynskyi — known in Yiddish as Zvhil — became a major center of Hasidism, and the Zvhil dynasty of Hasidic rebbes originated here; the oldest surviving matzevah in this cemetery, dated 1855, belongs to R. Yechiel Michl Goldman of Zvhil, tied to that same lineage. During the pogroms of July–August 1919, the city was burned to the ground and about 1,000 Jews killed, despite organized Jewish self-defense groups; the victims were buried in mass graves in this cemetery. Soviet authorities later demolished the town's older Jewish cemetery, and Germans demolished some tombstones here during WWII for construction material; the remains of Holocaust victims from several nearby villages were reinterred here in the 1950s and 60s. In 2005, the long-lost grave of Mordechai Zeev Feierberg — one of the pioneering figures of modern Hebrew literature, who died in 1899 at just 25 — was rediscovered here. The cemetery was renovated in 2015, with a new fence financed by Bank Hapoalim of Israel.
